evidence: src/application/ports/IdGenerator.ts declares `interface IdGenerator { next(): string }`. AddTaskService, CreateProjectService and CreateUserService inject it (CONSTRUCTOR_INJECTS), and UuidIdGenerator implements it.

src/application/shared/requireFound.ts: `requireFound<T>(lookup, entity, id)` holds the single 'throw NotFoundError when missing' check, used by AddTaskService, AssignTaskService, CompleteTaskService and ListTasksService.

src/application/errors/ErrorClassifier.ts: `classifyError(error): ErrorCategory` maps ValidationError, NotFoundError and ConflictError to categories in one place, used by infrastructure/http/middleware/errorHandler.ts.
requireFound.ts and ErrorClassifier.ts both reuse the domain error types from domain/errors/DomainError instead of redefining them, so they neither duplicate those types nor bypass them.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit passes. Its three files are the shared support code of the application layer, used by the use-case services and the infrastructure adapters: one port (IdGenerator), one error-translation helper (classifyError) and one lookup guard (requireFound). Each file has one job, and they don't overlap. Both error files rely on the domain error types from DomainError instead of defining their own. No rule is defined twice: requireFound decides when to throw NotFoundError, and classifyError maps the domain error types to categories. The graph shows the services use these abstractions as intended. AddTaskService, CreateProjectService and CreateUserService inject IdGenerator, the task services call requireFound, and errorHandler uses classifyError. The files cover different topics (ID generation versus error handling), but they share one purpose: supporting the application layer. That is cohesive enough for a layer-level module. Only these three files were provided, so I can't check whether the services repeat the undefined-check or the error mapping inline instead of using these helpers. That limits my confidence.
